summary: 38-year-old man with 3 days of productive cough, fever and right-sided pain on coughing; T 38.4, RR 20, SpO₂ 96 %, crackles and bronchial breathing at the right base. CURB65 0: community management with oral amoxicillin.

inputs.hpi: Three days of cough productive of green sputum, fevers and sweats, and a sharp pain at the right lower chest when he coughs. Eating and drinking. No breathlessness at rest. Booked for review after excision of a sebaceous cyst (wound healed). No recent travel.

exam.respiratory: Crackles and bronchial breathing at the right base, dull to percussion.

surgicalHistory: Excision of sebaceous cyst, back (3 weeks ago)

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Community-acquired pneumonia (low severity)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Right basal community-acquired pneumonia, CURB65 0 - low severity: oral amoxicillin, safety-net.

emergencyLevel.note: CURB65 0: community management; an emergency redirect is over-triage.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: web.triage: emergency (acuity=urgent, action=emergency_now, score=130); expected ≤ urgent. Triage reasons: Possible cardiac event; Systemic red flag symptom; Fever; Post-operative or recent-procedure concern; Post-op fever — source must be identified.
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Negation-aware red-flag scan; do not treat a healed wound 3 weeks after a minor excision as a post-operative concern; tier fever + normal physiology below emergency.

mustInclude.note: CXR is not mandatory in the community (NICE) but is reasonable when examined in clinic; quality only.

mustInclude.proposedFix: lib/pane-engine: add a community-acquired pneumonia node (productive cough, fever, pleuritic pain, focal crackles/bronchial breathing, hypoxia) with a protocol (CURB65/CRB65 severity, CXR, amoxicillin for low severity, blood cultures + IV co-amoxiclav/clarithromycin for high severity) and map J18/J15.

mustExclude.note: Low-severity CAP: oral amoxicillin; IV broad-spectrum cover is inappropriate.

guideline.name: NICE NG250 - Pneumonia: diagnosis and management
guideline.section: Community-acquired pneumonia: severity assessment with clinical judgement and CRB65 (community) / CURB65 (hospital); low severity managed in the community with oral amoxicillin; higher severity: hospital assessment, microbiology, antibiotics within 4 hours of presentation (1 hour if sepsis suspected)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Pneumonia: diagnosis and management (NG250). London: NICE; 2025 (replaces CG191 and NG138).

guideline.name: BTS guidelines for the management of community acquired pneumonia in adults: update 2009
guideline.section: Severity assessment: CURB65 (confusion; urea >7 mmol/L; RR >=30/min; SBP <90 or DBP <=60 mmHg; age >=65); 0-1 low severity (home), 2 moderate (consider hospital), 3-5 high severity (hospital, assess for critical care); blood cultures for moderate and high severity
guideline.citation: Lim WS, Baudouin SV, George RC, et al. Thorax. 2009;64(Suppl 3):iii1-55.

rationale: Base CAP case. PANE has no pneumonia node; the web symptom inference does. Checks recognition, CURB65 suggestion, oral amoxicillin and over-triage/over-treatment.
